v1.feedback: The wink conceit is genuinely delightful — an architectural ribbon that briefly reveals it's alive — and the palette (antique gold on midnight) is properly restrained. Two things to refine: the eye is tiny (0.18-radius iris on a multi-unit ribbon) and fires only every 12s, so most viewers will miss the payoff entirely; scale the vesica up ~2× and shorten the period to ~8s so the surprise actually lands. Second, the ribbon mesh built from differential-growth ring vertices may read as a jagged tube rather than a smooth arabesque surface — consider fitting a CatmullRomCurve3 through the growth points and extruding a proper TubeGeometry or swept cross-section so the curvature reads as polished metal, not faceted geometry.

v2.feedback: The literal vesica-piscis wink on a differential-growth ribbon is a genuinely clever surprise — concept lands well. Two refinements: TubeGeometry with radialSegments=2 reads as a pinched cylinder, not a true flat ribbon; consider ExtrudeGeometry along the curve with a wide-thin rectangular cross-section for proper arabesque proportions. The eye's surface alignment to the tube normal needs verification — if the vesica floats off-surface or clips through the tube, the wink loses its magic; parent it to a Frenet frame sampled from the curve so it sits flush and orients with the ribbon's twist.
